pr_title: drivers: pinctrl: Add ZynqMP / Mercury XU pinctrl support
pr_body:
This PR removes the custom pin control setup from the `board.c` file for the Mercury XU platform and replaces it with an implementation compliant with the `pinctrl` specification.

Fixes #52437

issue_context.title: drivers: pinctrl: add pinctrl driver for the Xilinx ZynqMP platform
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
As noted in #39740 the Xilinx ZynqMP platform uses a custom pinctrl driver (as seen in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/boards/arm/mercury_xu/board.c).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The Xilinx ZynqMP platform should use one of the standard Zephyr pinctrl devicetree representations as described in https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/pinctrl/index.html#devicetree-representation along with a pinctrl driver.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None.

**Additional context**
See the Xilinx Zynq-7000 series pinctrl binding + driver for inspiration.

review_comments: driver does not use any DT APIs, other than the redundant line below.
Now it does use DT API to fetch the MIO Register base address. Should it be removed despite that?
Yes, that's unused, but I think it should be left here. It defines the layout of the register. One less thing to check for the next person using it.
dead code is not allowed in Zephyr
I don't think this qualifies as dead code. A lot of device drivers and SoCs define all of their registers and fields, even if they are not used yet.

Hi @henrikbrixandersen, @gmarull! It looks like the discussion here has been stalled for some time now.

We’ve originally added the `MIO_L1_SEL` field definition for reasons stated by @henrikbrixandersen, but we’re okay with either way - keeping this define or removing it altogether.

Let us know how we should proceed with this. Thanks!
Ok, it won't hurt, it's just a single definition with potential future use within pinctrl_soc.h.
